name: ふみちゃん 流川店 (Fumi-chan Nagarekawa-ten)

claims.text: All okonomiyaki are cooked together on a shared teppan (griddle) where wheat batter and wheat noodles are constantly handled, so cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable.
Dishes are finished with okonomiyaki/Mitsuwa sauce and a soy-sauce-and-vinegar ponzu, both of which are conventionally wheat-containing.
The same griddle is used for pork, egg and noodles, so any vegetable item would share surfaces with animal ingredients.

name: 元祖へんくつや 本店 (Ganso Henkutsuya Honten)

claims.text: Okonomiyaki is cooked on a shared teppan griddle alongside wheat batter and wheat noodles, so wheat cross-contact is unavoidable.
Hiroshima okonomiyaki is finished with okonomiyaki sauce, which is typically made with wheat-based soy sauce; no gluten-free sauce is indicated.
Dishes are cooked on a communal griddle with egg, pork and seafood, so vegan dishes cannot be reliably separated.

name: ガーデンハウス ヒロシマ (GARDEN HOUSE HIROSHIMA)

claims.text: Kitchen centers on a wood-fired oven for pizza and serves pasta and pancakes, so flour is used heavily throughout; no gluten-free handling is documented.
A vegan/vegetarian menu is offered, including a falafel and vegetable plate, giving plant-based diners a clear option.
Core drinks are made from a homemade syrup of just Hiroshima lemons (peel and juice) and sugar via an anhydrous method, so the signature lemonades and sodas are simple and plant-based by ingredient.
Lemons are sourced from pesticide-free / contract farms in Setoda, Hiroshima, with the whole fruit used in the syrup.

name: 五エ門 胡町本店 (Goemon Ebisucho Honten)

claims.text: Okonomiyaki is cooked on a shared teppan grill alongside wheat-flour batter and wheat noodles, so gluten contact is unavoidable across the menu.
Okonomiyaki sauce typically contains wheat; no gluten-free sauce is documented for this restaurant.
Dishes are grilled on a communal teppan shared with pork, egg, and seafood (oysters, anago), making vegan separation impractical.

Signature dishes are built on wheat-flour tortillas (burritos, soft tacos, enchiladas) and several items are battered and deep-fried (fish tacos, chimichangas), so gluten exposure and shared-fryer cross-contact are likely; no gluten-free protocol is documented.

Vegetarian dishes can reportedly be made vegan on request, but Mexican dishes here commonly include cheese and sour cream and the kitchen is meat/fish-heavy, so confirm omission of dairy and animal fats when ordering.
Staff are described as very friendly and have indicated they can adapt vegetarian dishes to vegan, suggesting willingness to accommodate requests communicated at the table.
Everything is made from scratch in-house, including the fresh salsa and guacamole, which makes plant-based customization easier to request.

The owner-chef states he tailors dishes to customer preferences rather than imposing a set menu, so accommodation requests can be discussed directly; however, no specific allergy or gluten/vegan handling procedures are documented.
Vegetables are the centerpiece of the cooking, with many seasonal vegetable dishes available.

name: 餃子家 龍 新天地本店 (Gyozaya Ryu Shintenchi Honten)

claims.text: A wheat-heavy kitchen producing pan-fried wheat-flour gyoza, fried items and noodle-style dishes; gluten cross-contact is very likely and no gluten-free handling is advertised.
Standard Japanese/Chinese soy sauce and sauces are used across the menu (e.g., okonomiyaki-sauce gyoza); these contain wheat. No wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned.
Gyoza are pork-filled and most dishes are meat- or seafood-based with soy/dashi seasonings cooked on shared equipment; no vegan preparation is documented.
